For ARG41's NH2 atom, I need to exclude CZ, NE, and NH1 since they're within two bonds, then check nearby candidates like CD to find the closest qualifying protein heavy atom.

Working through the distances, ARG41's own CD atom (three bonds away, so allowed) comes out to about 2.82 Å, closer than anything from GLN50, GLU67, ASP48, or other nearby residues I checked. Let me also verify against LEU42's backbone nitrogen before settling on CD as the answer.

I want to double-check this though — 2.82 Å seems tight for a CD-NH2 distance across the guanidinium group, since typical CD-NH1/CD-NH2 separations depend on the dihedral orientation of the planar group, so I'm recomputing the CD coordinates to make sure this checks out.

Confirming the distance calculation gives roughly 2.819 Å, matching what I found before. Now I'm scanning through nearby atoms to see if anything else falls within that same radius, checking each residue's coordinates against the bounding box to rule out closer contacts.

After checking neighboring atoms in ARG39, ASP48, LEU42, and GLU67, none fall within the box, confirming CD as the closest atom. So my answer settles on A:R41:CD, though I pause to reconsider whether the intended exclusion criteria might be different, but the instructions specify excluding only one or two bonds, so I'll stick with this result.
